title: SafeBench-Seq: A Homology-Clustered CPU-Only Baseline for Protein Hazard Screening
author: (arXiv 2512.17527)
summary: Public benchmark built from SafeProtein hazards and UniProt benigns; homology-clustered at <=40% identity with cluster-level holdouts to approximate never-before-seen threats. Provides a CPU-only baseline using physicochemical and composition features.
notes: Closest fit to the hackathon problem; gives ready-made train/test with the exact AI-evasion setup we want SAE features evaluated against.

title: The Limits of Sequence-Based Biosecurity Screening Tools in the Age of AI-Assisted Protein Design
author: (bioRxiv)
summary: Documents how AI-redesigned variants evade current sequence-based screening; motivates the need for representation-based detectors.
notes: Frames the threat model. Useful for the writeup and to source adversarial examples to test against.

title: Strengthening nucleic acid biosecurity screening against generative protein design tools
author: (Science)
summary: Red-team study evaluating open-source AI protein design tools generating evasive variants of proteins of concern; resulted in patches deployed to screening tools.
notes: Companion to the bioRxiv paper; the canonical reference for the AI-evasion vulnerability the hackathon track is responding to.

title: ToxinPred 3.0: An improved method for predicting the toxicity of peptides
author: (Raghava lab)
summary: Balanced peptide-level toxic vs non-toxic classifier dataset. Negatives sourced from UniProt with 'NOT toxin NOT toxic AND reviewed:yes'; peptides <35 aa.
notes: Peptide-only (short sequences); good for warm-up baselines but won't cover protein-length toxins.

title: ToxinPred2: an improved method for predicting toxicity of proteins
author: (Raghava lab)
summary: Protein-length toxic vs non-toxic dataset with Main / Alternate / Realistic splits. Realistic split closest to deployment conditions.
notes: Use the Realistic split for evaluation; Main split for training. Protein-length so directly compatible with RFD3 inputs.

title: Towards a Dataset for State of the Art Protein Toxin Classification (BioLMTox)
author: (bioRxiv)
summary: Unified toxin classifier (BioLMTox) trained on a merged corpus consolidating prior toxin datasets; current SOTA single-model baseline.
notes: Use as the baseline to beat with SAE-feature classifiers.

title: Victors: a web-based knowledge base of virulence factors in human and animal pathogens
author: (NAR)
summary: Manually curated virulence factors from >100 bacterial, viral, parasitic, and fungal pathogens.
notes: Includes viral entries (unlike PHI-base). No native benign class — pair with UniProt `reviewed:yes NOT virulence` as negatives.

title: VFDB: Virulence Factor Database
author: (mgc.ac.cn / NAR)
summary: Reference database of bacterial virulence factors with continually expanded orthologues and alleles.
notes: Bacterial-only; well-curated. Same UniProt-negative pairing trick for benigns.

title: PHI-base: the multi-species pathogen-host interaction database in 2025
author: (NAR)
summary: Experimentally verified pathogenicity, virulence, and effector genes from fungal, protist, and bacterial pathogens.
notes: Does NOT include viral pathogens — Victors is preferred if viral coverage matters.

title: SecureDNA features
author: (SecureDNA Foundation)
summary: Free non-profit DNA synthesis screening; detects hazards down to 30 bp / 20 aa using a 'random adversarial threshold' search over functional variants.
notes: Reference deployed system; not a dataset but defines the bar a detector should exceed. The screening hashes are not public, but the threat model is.

title: AI-designed proteins test biosecurity safeguards
author: (Science News)
summary: Lay-press summary of the Science red-team study; useful one-pager for context.
notes: Quick read for non-technical context — good for the writeup intro.
